newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba's Jochimsen criticises EU report on EMU.
newsitem.headline: Buba's Jochimsen criticises EU report on EMU.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Reimut Jochimsen sharply criticised a report by the European Commission outlining prospects for membership in the planned European currency union, a newspaper said on Thursday.

Jochimsen told Germany's Handelsblatt newspaper that he targeted the report for being overly generous in prospects for countries seeking to join the currency, which is slated to be launched in January 1999.

"The really noticeable thing is that the European Commission, with its report and very generous outlook, has not realised that it is the protector of the Maastricht Treaty," he said in the interview released in advance of publication on Friday.
He said the treaty was there to secure a lasting and stable currency union, not one that falls apart at the first opportunity.
Jochimsen said in an advance release of the newspaper article that the Maastricht Treaty did not require exact numerical fulfillment but instead required that the sense of the treaty be fulfilled.
He said the most important target was price stability.
